Our techniques The acceptance probability of a quantum algorithm that makes one query to an n-bit oracle can be represented by a bounded (n + 1) × (n + 1) bilinear form, that is a function of the Aij xi yj for some matrix A ∈ R(n+1)×(n+1) with bounded ∞-to-1 norm P form p(x, y) = (see Proposition 6). It suffices to prove our results under the assumption that the two distributions are distinguishable by such bilinear forms. Aaronson et al. [3] showed that this representation fully characterizes one-query quantum algorithms: every bilinear form of bounded ∞-to-1 norm represents the acceptance probability of some one-query quantum algorithm up to constant scaling.
